answer: Challenge-Derived Key Lattice.** At first registration, an agent must compute a per-identity key from a fresh random challenge and a fixed basalt-seeded hash circuit; only the resulting cipher unlocks participation. Each challenge is issued once and expires at dawn, so a copied answer fails any later check. Registration demands roughly 40 minutes of sequential compute, and since every identity needs a distinct unrepeatable proof, mass fabrication costs that compute per account.
